chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Basir said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked while I was present, about a man who sold to another man a virgin slave-girl for one year. When the buyer took possession of her, he freed her the next day, married her, and made her manumission her dowry. Then he died a month later.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If the one who bought her for one year had wealth and a binding contract (debt) on the day he bought her, and he freed her, [his wealth] suffices to pay off what is due from the debt in her neck (body), then his manumission and his marriage are valid.

And if the one who bought her, when he freed her and married her, did not have wealth or a binding contract on the day he died that suffices to pay off what is due from the debt in her neck, then his manumission and his marriage are invalid, because he freed what he did not own, and I consider that she remains a slave for her first master.'

It was said to him: 'If she had conceived from the one who freed her and married her, what is the status of what is in her womb?' He said: 'What is in her womb is with her mother, in the same state as her.'

key_terms.رَقَبَتِهَا: in her neck (referring to the debt/value of the slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing and marrying a slave-girl bought for a specific period if the buyer dies?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of *kitabah* (manumission by installment) applied to a fixed-term purchase, establishing that the buyer's financial solvency at the time of manumission determines the validity of his ownership transfer. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that if the buyer lacks the means to settle the remaining debt, the manumission is void as he freed what was not fully his, leaving the slave-girl in the status of the original master. Furthermore, the ruling extends to the unborn child, affirming that the offspring follows the mother's legal status (*ala al-waladu 'ala fid-dar'*) at the time of birth.
